conventions.bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1], fractions of the PDF page (A4, incl. the white frame around the scan)

drawings.description: à gauche, un dessin de graphe : une douzaine de sommets marqués d'un point, des arêtes droites et courbes, deux arêtes doubles joignant les mêmes sommets, une arête isolée et un sommet isolé
drawings.kind: graph with multiple edges, an isolated edge and an isolated vertex
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop, the bbox raised by 0.01 to take in the top vertex (a dot, with the curved edge down to the junction at the upper right, both missing before). Every edge is drawn between the same computed vertices. Dots where the page has them (ten: the top vertex, the vertex at the upper right end, the upper centre, the right, the middle, the central, the lower right vertices, the isolated vertex and both ends of the isolated edge); the junctions without a dot (upper right, the left corner of the lens, its inner end, the vertex under the central one, the bottom) are drawn as plain meetings of strokes. Edges: a lens of two curves from the upper centre vertex (one sweeping left to the left corner, the other going down and then left to the inner end), the inner end joined to the left corner and to the central vertex; a double edge of two curves from the central vertex down to the bottom, where the straight edge from the vertex under the central one also ends. Left out: a short smudged stroke at the lower right, the caption under the figure (text). Still partial: the graph is not encoded (the vertices without dots make the vertex set a reading). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question closed by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (no consequence): the sketch is an example of a graph with double edges, an isolated edge and an isolated vertex; whether the junctions without a clear dot count as vertices does not change what it shows, and the dots are drawn where the page has them. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 350 dpi colour render of the scan. Every vertex, dot and edge lies on the ink to within about 0.5 unit, except the outer curve of the lens, which ran up to 2 units above its ink and is now drawn through points read on it. The short smudged stroke at the lower right, left out before, is drawn as the stroke it is (a stray mark beside the graph, not one of its edges). The graph is drawn, not encoded: the junctions without a dot are drawn as plain meetings of strokes, as on the page (the question of which of them count as vertices was closed on 2026-11-12). Left out: the caption under the figure (text).

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, deux dessins : au crayon, un contour à deux sommets et deux arêtes ; à l'encre, un pentagone
drawings.kind: contour with two vertices and two edges; pentagon
drawings.notes: A contour of two vertices joined by two edges (a lens), and a pentagon with marked vertices. On the render the lens is the heavier stroke and the pentagon the lighter one, the reverse of what the transcription says (pencil lens, ink pentagon); both are drawn as on the page.
drawings.disagreement: The lens (contour with two vertices) is heavily inked and the pentagon light, not pencil lens and ink pentagon.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, deux petits dessins : deux arcs orientés mis bout à bout, puis un arc de $s$ vers $u_\omega(s)$ marqué $\sigma^{-1}s$ ; plus bas, l'arc $a$ d'origine $\sigma a$ suivi de l'arc $u_\omega(a)$, d'origine $\sigma u_\omega(a)$
drawings.kind: oriented arcs: s to u_omega(s); a followed by u_omega(a)
drawings.notes: Top: two oriented arcs end to end. Then an arc from s towards u_omega(s), marked sigma^{-1}s. Lower: the arc a with origin sigma a, followed by the arc u_omega(a) with origin sigma u_omega(a). The small labels are placed after the transcription.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, au crayon, un petit dessin : un segment oblique épais entre deux points marqués, prolongé au-delà du second par un trait fin.
drawings.kind: segment between two marked points, on a line
drawings.notes: Left margin, pencil, beside « l'image d'une arête soit un segment ». A heavy oblique segment between two full points; beyond the upper point the same straight line goes on as a thin stroke, with a small mark at its end; the three points are computed on one line. Disagreement in part with the note of the transcription (« un segment dont les deux extrémités sont marquées »): the stroke does not stop at the second marked point. Nothing struck. Id 01-4: existing ids are not renumbered. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the segment, its two marked points and the thin continuation match; the thin stroke starts a little beyond the upper point, leaving a small gap as on the page (corrected). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, un petit dessin : deux segments formant un angle.
drawings.kind: two segments forming an angle (two sides of a polygon at a vertex)
drawings.notes: Left margin, beside the paragraph on regular polygons. Two straight strokes, one rising gently from the lower left, one steep, forming an obtuse angle; they are drawn meeting at one computed vertex (on the page a gap of about two units is left between their ends). Nothing struck. Id 01-5: existing ids are not renumbered. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the two segments match the page; nothing corrected. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
